ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a structure containing a five-membered saturated ring; the nitrogen in the ring is labeled as positively charged, and the nitrogen is also connected to a negatively charged oxygen atom; the other substituent of the nitrogen is a methylene connected to a cyano group. On the right side there is a chiral ring carbon with a solid wedge bond, and this carbon is connected to a -CH2-O-CH2- fragment, then connected to a methyl-substituted terminal alkene fragment at the lower right. The curved arrows in the figure indicate transition-state electron movement, but the question requires ignoring the arrows and transcribing only the molecular connectivity. Reasoning: Starting from the terminal alkene/methyl allyl fragment at the lower right, it can be written as C=C(C)C; this fragment is connected through oxygen to methylene, giving C=C(C)COC; this methylene is then connected to the chiral five-membered ring carbon with solid-wedge configuration, encoded according to the given traversal as [C@@H]1; continuing along the saturated five-membered ring gives CCC, and it closes to the positively charged ring nitrogen; this nitrogen is written as [N+]1, and is simultaneously connected to oxide anion [O-] and the cyanomethyl substituent CC#N. Therefore the complete SMILES is C=C(C)COC[C@@H]1CCC[N+]1([O-])CC#N.

method.method_draft: First describe the image connectivity: ignore the curved arrows and transcribe only the molecular graph. Start from the terminal alkene/methallyl fragment as C=C(C)C, connect it through oxygen to a methylene as C=C(C)COC, then attach that CH2 to the chiral ring carbon. Encode that chiral ring carbon with the solid-wedge configuration in the chosen traversal as [C@@H]1, continue around the saturated five-membered ring as CCC, and close at the ring nitrogen. Write the ring nitrogen as positively charged and substituted by oxide and cyanomethyl: [N+]1([O-])CC#N. Concatenating these fragments gives C=C(C)COC[C@@H]1CCC[N+]1([O-])CC#N.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是一个含五元饱和环的结构，环内氮标为正电荷，氮还连有一个带负电的氧原子；氮的另一取代基是一个亚甲基连接到氰基。右侧有一个带实楔键的手性环碳，该碳连接到一个 -CH2-O-CH2- 片段，再接到右下方的甲基取代末端烯烃片段。图中的弯箭头表示过渡态电子移动，但题目要求忽略箭头，只转录分子连接关系。
推理：从右下方末端烯烃/甲基烯丙基片段开始，可写为 C=C(C)C；该片段通过氧连接到亚甲基，得到 C=C(C)COC；该亚甲基再连接到带实楔构型的手性五元环碳，按给定遍历编码为 [C@@H]1；沿饱和五元环继续为 CCC，并闭合到带正电的环氮；该氮写作 [N+]1，同时连有氧负离子 [O-] 和氰甲基取代基 CC#N。因此完整 SMILES 为 C=C(C)COC[C@@H]1CCC[N+]1([O-])CC#N。

planner_metadata.image_role: Read the skeletal structure while ignoring all curved arrows: identify a five-membered pyrrolidine ring containing a positively charged N, with an N-oxide [N+]([O-]); an N-substituent CH2-CN; a stereocenter on the ring carbon bearing a solid wedge to a CH2-O substituent; and an ether side chain O-CH2-C(CH3)=CH2.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question instruction that the requested output is the SMILES expression of the shown transition-state structure and that the arrows should be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply standard SMILES rules: implicit carbons in skeletal drawings, explicit formal charges as [N+] and [O-], nitrile as C#N, alkene as C=C(C), ring closure digits for the pyrrolidine ring, and tetrahedral stereochemistry from the wedge using the chosen atom order as [C@@H].
